headline: Anupama Ramachandran Beats So Man Yan 3-1 to Defend World Snooker Title
subheadline: The 3-1 win in Indore makes Anupama the first Indian to win back-to-back IBSF world snooker crowns, a year after her maiden title in Doha.
body:
• Anupama Ramachandran beat Hong Kong China's So Man Yan 3-1 in Indore on Saturday to retain her IBSF World Snooker Championship title.
  • She is the first Indian to win back-to-back world snooker crowns, having won her maiden title in Doha in November 2025.
  • After dropping the first frame 16-58, she won the next three 83-7, 85-26 and 65-37, and earned USD 4,000 for the title.
  • In the men's final, Iran's Ali Gharahgozlou beat Hong Kong China's Tam Yun Fung 5-1; Pankaj Advani lost his semi-final 3-5.

Anupama Ramachandran defended her IBSF World Snooker Championship title in Indore on Saturday, beating Hong Kong China's So Man Yan 3-1 in the final to become the first Indian to win back-to-back world snooker crowns, according to India Today.

The final, played at the Yeshwant Club in Indore, did not start her way. Anupama lost a scrappy opening frame 16-58, then found her rhythm and took control of the match. She levelled with an 83-7 frame built on runs of 31, 19 and 16, moved ahead 2-1 with an 85-26 frame, and closed out the match 65-37, potting a long blue to the bottom-right pocket and the pink to the top-right to seal the title, The Bridge reported.

How she got there

Anupama reached the final with two 3-1 wins, beating fellow Indian Keerthana Pandian in the quarter-finals and England's Tessa Davidson in the semi-finals, according to The Bridge. The title earned her USD 4,000.

Speaking after the event, she said defending the title was even more special than winning it the first time, and that doing it on home soil made it memorable. A year ago in Doha, she beat Ng On-yee 3-2 to become the first Indian woman to win the IBSF world snooker title. Her earlier international titles include the 2023 Women's Snooker World Cup, won with Amee Kamani, the 2023 World Women's Under-21 Championship and the 2024 Asian Women's Snooker Championship.

Advani falls short in the men's event

India's wait for a men's world champion at this event continues. Pankaj Advani, a three-time champion and the last Indian man to win the title, in 2017, lost his semi-final 3-5 to Iran's Ali Gharahgozlou, The Bridge reported. Gharahgozlou went on to beat Hong Kong China's Tam Yun Fung 5-1 in the final and take the USD 10,000 winner's cheque. Three other Indians — Brijesh Damani, Digvijay Kadian and Dhvaj Haria — lost in the quarter-finals.

The Chennai-born 24-year-old also plays the World Women's Snooker tour, where she reached a career-high ranking of sixth in March 2025 and her first ranking final at the 2024 US Women's Open. No next fixture for Anupama was announced in the reports of the final. What is settled is the record: two world titles in two years, the second of them defended at home.
